what: Dustin's quiz answers, run 3 (artifact RLNHNAwm55DpVLe1JniuJC, db collection answers), read by the coordinator with ArtifactData on 2026-10-25 after he said he had finished

answers.note: Okay on this I can't see what the retreat cost for gouging fire was, but hypothetically the opponent could retreat gouging fire to rayquaza, use dragonair's ability and attach energy from it and their energy from their turn. If they have rainbow stadium they can discard another energy and theoretically could use flame patch, dragonair's ability and their energy to get 3 additional energies onto mega rayquaza. So they could do 150 or 200 damage to mega sableye ex, who if they die, I lose. My idea with retreating was using hoopa's ability to damage their mega who I'm going to have to kill anyway and protect my mega, who isn't accomplishing much attacking a one point pokemon and not even killing him. I would be curious to know if one was definitely better than the other.

I think either is acceptable, but mine was better... I don't remember how this one played out so from this snapshot, leaving espeon active is ensuring that hoopa ex dies next turn. Pulling darkrai up with only one energy means he can't attack or retreat without xspeed/leaf and usually they are stuck with a wasted turn and I would be able to hopefully keep hoopa alive and be able to attack with it next turn. There is also no guarantee that you would kill espeon with two darkrai abilities, they might have healing tools or supporters. I'm fairly confident my move is the best, but not 100% sure

I'm not sure why you aren't showing me their attacks and retreat costs... My thinking is that I'm hoping I'm able to retreat grimer with the cheaper retreat costs, before evolving him to either muk. Non ex muk would maybe have been the play if I was facing a different deck that had basic pokemon with abilities, Muk ex would have probably been my last choice. The odds of him surviving two more turns after this one where he would be able to attack seem low and I would be giving up 2 points with a small chance of using him. If I'm not able to use the evolved pokemon and evolving the current one isn't going to give me a clear advantage (like if the attacking pokemon was going to do 90 damage to 80 hp grimer), giving up one point is better than two. This is also a deck I wasn't super familiar with, but I think that was the correct move... I can't really imagine a scenario where the other line turns out better over a whole game.

They already had 1 point, were going to get a second point on their next turn killing dustox. My strategy was to work on getting muk ex able to attack to have a chance with his attack. Dustox's attack wouldn't have killed butterfree and butterfree heals with its attack. I think there are only bad options and we are losing either way, so dealers choice?

answers.choice: The alternative was better (my play was a mistake)
answers.note: I think the other play would have been better. Getting one point for killing carbink, being able to survive diancie's attack, and then using cyrus to kill flutter mane next turn seems like the obviously better move. I don't remember diancies attack exactly so unless they were killing me either way next turn, the other line was the better option.

Why would you attach water to sharpedo that already has 1 energy that it needs to attack and free retreat costs? This is also a lost cause most likely, but leaving sharpedo up, ensures you lose next turn because they have a 2nd vespiqueen ex ready to kill you. Retreating keeps you alive a little longer if they don't have a cyrus...

I think my thinking is the odds of me getting something helpful from copycat and being able to evolve carvanha with either wallace or redrawing mega sharpedo was the better play. Cyrus wasn't going to be helpful and so you are giving up mega sharpedo ex for a chance at drawing 4 new cards. Wailmer is stuck up front anyway so you can't switch in mega sharpedo ex next turn anyway, if you could that would change my mind.

The other line here seems to value the second point, but that is worthless when they are about to get 3 points and win the game. But a move I see now that I'm unsure why I didn't do would be to retreat and put goomy in the active spot, since I have one card left to draw and it is a second flygon that I could evolve and use next turn. Playing cyrus and retreating to goomy might have been the best move.

Upon reflection, I think retreating would have been the smartest move. I think I was trying to take the kill, but retreating to goomy might have been the best move. The opponent would then have had to waste their next energy attaching it to happiny, or retreat and attack with riolu and wouldn't have been able to attack with lucario. This would have given me time to get the dragonair for the energy attaching ability or just the turn based energy I needed to get flygon ready to attack, before exposing him to the danger.

Well this seems to be a new engine repair finding. Dragon's blessing only works if the dragonair is on the bench. You can't use it on yourself so their line isn't possible in real life.

I think my thinking was if the active trapinch could sacrifice themselves, I could get the bench one started and if I drew flygon with my next turn, I already had the rare candy and could use dragonair's ability to finish his energy and be able to attack the next turn

Honestly not sure. My thinking was, the only way to win this is to kill their mega. Doing damage to butterfree is virtually worthless unless I kill it, which the other line wouldn't do. Then they use butterfree's attack, do 60 damage, I then either have to switch to someone else, but also they now have damaged my ex and can use cyrus at any time to pull him up and kill him in one shot with mega sceptile. Retreating and attacking with buzzwole maybe would have been the best move, but my logic was using pheromosa does damage to sceptile and that is the only way to win.

It's not obvious, but I think my play was better. Hitmonlee attacks the bench and both the benched eiscue and wartortle are protected, so the water attaching to oricorio was to help it survive another two attacks. But the other option is acceptable and losing oricorio doesn't significantly hurt you here.

I don't see the harm in waiting a turn to use the boosted attack, but I think you could have won either way since you had the cyrus? I think waiting until he has 6 energies is the smarter move, but don't really know that the difference is much

Fairly confident my move was better. You waste an energy putting it on eiscue to save a point that doesn't matter. What matters is getting blastoise online and powered up. I think this an example of the bot valuing one point, but not seeing how to win the game

Once again, the only way you win is getting blastoise with enough energy, the other line waste an energy to put the more valuable pokemon into a vulnerable position. I think that is the worst move possible. That being said, switching to bench eiscue wouldn't have been unreasonable

My logic, Entei would likely do 60 damage next turn against 140 hp, I can heal with indeedee or lillie next turn. Once Entei gets 4 energy attached he does 120 damage and it would be better to use cheren against a 120 attack over a 60 attack. That was my thinking, I think both moves are reasonable with the given information

answers.choice: The alternative was better (my play was a mistake)
answers.note: Yeah this was an unfamiliar deck and I didn't know what I was doing. I think we are losing no matter what, but terapagos ex does come on quicker and could do 140 damage if we attach three different energies.

answers.choice: The alternative was better (my play was a mistake)
answers.note: My thinking was that goomy made their attack cost more and was going to die with the next turn anyway. After I switched I realized that sacrificing an energy for 10 hp of damage (20 damage to the bench versus 30 to the active) wasn't worth it. I believe the next turn he cyrus'ed my haxorus back up and so I got the worst of both, lost energy and full damage...

answers.choice: The alternative was better (my play was a mistake)
answers.note: Okay what I was thinking was that if I knocked the hydreigon out, there was a decent chance he was going to evolve his deino into a new one next turn and finish me off. Moving oricorio was a way to sacrifice a point and perhaps heal more and give me more of a chance to make a move. I think if I had this example come up again, I would kill the known hydreigon and take my chances because that was the only option that might lead to victory.

I think either is fine. With this deck, I weighed the chances I would get something useful (wallace or the sharpedo back) above the chances I would get a brick deck. Sharpedo by himself isn't that helpful, he is useful for getting water energy onto the bench. An elegant cape by itself isn't helpful either. So it was just a calculation on whether my current hand was better than random chance at a couple cards from the deck

I think my plan was better because if sharpedo dies, you lose, but there was no guarantee that you would draw sharpedo so I understand the other line. I have just found that the extra 30 hp on sharpedo can make the difference between winning/losing and I wasn't as concerned with keeping milotic alive

answers.choice: The alternative was better (my play was a mistake)
answers.note: I think I saw it after I attached the water, but that would have been better because gyarados also discards their top 3 cards.

Attacking is completely fine and the right move if you need the energy. The carvanha on the bench doesn't need more energy. It is rare, but some pokemon's attacks scale with how many energies are attached, so I don't always use every energy if it doesn't help me in any way. Free retreat and one energy attacks means I don't ever need more than 1 unless they have the ability to steal energy
